rules.rule: Check for urgent peripheral vascular disease conditions
rules.problem: Trigger is PVD, which fits the red-box heading. The check_for covers every red-box finding. BP is a routine vital, so leaving it out is correct.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable acute limb ischaemia in peripheral vascular disease
rules.problem: "Likely" maps to probable. The structure is sudden severe rest pain AND any of (numbness, weakness, pallor, no pulse) in the leg, which matches the page.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable critical limb ischaemia in peripheral vascular disease
rules.problem: Faithful OR of rest pain, leg ulcer and leg gangrene. Side effect: any acute-limb-ischaemia presentation (sudden severe pain at rest) also satisfies the rest-pain branch, so both diagnoses fire together. That follows the page wording but is worth a reviewer glance.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm in peripheral vascular disease
rules.problem: Reads "Pulsatile mass in abdomen with abdominal/back pain or BP < 90/60" as mass AND (pain OR low BP). That is the natural reading, though the page is grammatically ambiguous. Splitting BP<90/60 into systolic<90 OR diastolic<60 follows the gold standard, but diastolic<60 alone with a pulsatile mass is a broad trigger for "ruptured AAA likely".

rules.rule: Diagnose possible abdominal aortic aneurysm in peripheral vascular disease
rules.problem: Supported by the Assess table: "If pulsatile mass felt, refer for assessment for possible abdominal aortic aneurysm". "Possible" is the right level.

rules.rule: Urgent: peripheral vascular disease with acute/critical limb ischaemia or ruptured AAA
rules.problem: "Give urgent attention" maps to Urgent. The rule is PVD AND (any of the three probable diagnoses), which covers all three red-box bullets through their active_condition. The page gives no escalation to Emergency or Very urgent.

summary: No invented, wrong or misplaced conditions were found. Every rule traces to the red box or the Assess table, with the right probable/possible levels and Urgent priority. Minor points: the rest-pain encoding (c007/c021) could use the closer concept "Pain at rest due to peripheral vascular disease", and as written every acute-limb-ischaemia presentation also triggers critical limb ischaemia. The BP<90/60 split (diastolic<60 alone) makes "ruptured AAA likely" fire on a fairly common finding when a pulsatile mass is present.
